table.title: [val] Code · CLI flags
table.md:
| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--max-old-space-size` | number | `4096` | Sets the max memory size of V8's old memory section, in megabytes. |
| `--experimental-vm-modules` | boolean | `false` | Enables experimental ES module support in the `vm` module. |
| `-r`, `--require` | string | — | Preloads the specified module at startup. |
| `--inspect-brk=[host:]port` | string | `127.0.0.1:9229` | Activates inspector and breaks before user code starts. |

understanding.purpose: Document CLI flags so readers can choose an option and understand its type, default, and effect.
understanding.reading: Readers will scan flag names first, then read across the row to compare the type, default, and description. Descriptions can use multiple lines; those taller rows can also accommodate wrapped flag aliases.
groups: Flag identifies the option; Type and Default are compact attributes that belong together for comparison.
Description explains the effect of each flag and needs the most flexible width.
keep_intact: Individual flag names and placeholders, including --inspect-brk=[host]:port.
Type names and default values, especially 127.0.0.1:9229.
may_wrap: Multiple flag aliases within a cell, between the aliases.

preferred.name: r0C
preferred.note: Keep the full flag entries on one line to support rapid scanning, with descriptions taking more of the wrapping.

acceptable.name: r0A
acceptable.note: Balance readable flag names with a generous description column, allowing aliases and descriptions to wrap where needed.

bad.name: r0B
bad.note: Give descriptions the most space while retaining enough width for each individual flag name.
bad.why: The narrow flag column breaks long command-line options across three lines, making the identifiers harder to scan and copy. The resulting tall rows also weaken the relationship between each flag and its description.

rationale: r0C keeps every flag intact, making the first column a reliable index for scanning the table. Its descriptions wrap naturally to two lines, and the consistent body-row heights give each entry a clear rhythm. r0A gives descriptions more room, but splits several flags across lines.

general: Give identifiers enough width to remain intact when readers use them to locate or copy entries.
Allocate width according to each column's role and content rather than making columns equal.
specific: The Type and Default columns fit at 76px and 135px, leaving most of the width for flags and descriptions.
A 225px flag column accommodates the longest flag on one line, while descriptions remain readable at 283px.

tradeoffs: r0A is shorter and gives descriptions more horizontal space; r0C uses an extra line in one description to keep all flags intact.
uncertain: A designer who prioritizes compactness or reading descriptions over scanning flags could reasonably prefer r0A. The ranges are conservative estimates; they are not independently rendered, and changes must still fit within the 719px total.

critique.good: Type and Default are compact and easy to compare. Description has enough room for the shorter entry to stay on one line, and the rows remain reasonably compact.
critique.problems: Several flag names break across lines, making the primary scanning column harder to read and copy accurately.
critique.cause: The 180px Flag column is too narrow for the full flag names. The 328px Description column receives space that would be more useful keeping those identifiers intact.

critique.good: The wider Description column gives the explanatory text a comfortable measure, while Type and Default remain compact.
critique.problems: Long flag names fragment over two or three lines, weakening row scanning and producing tall rows with uneven whitespace.
critique.cause: The 127px Flag column leaves only 106px for text. Its width is insufficient for the longer identifiers, even though Description has 381px.

critique.good: Flag names, type names and defaults remain intact. The compact attribute columns sit together, and descriptions wrap into at most two lines. Rows read clearly as units with a consistent rhythm.
critique.problems: The shorter description wraps onto a second line, leaving some unused space in that row; the Description column is comparatively narrow.
critique.cause: The 225px Flag column reserves enough room for the longest complete flag, leaving 283px for Description within the width limit. That tradeoff supports the table’s primary scanning task.

review.method: two fresh-context blind reviews; letters shuffled; includes browser auto layout and equal widths as neutral references

r0B.why: The narrow Flag column breaks several command identifiers across lines, making them hard to scan and copy, while the description column has ample space.

r0C.why: Flags and defaults remain intact, the compact Type column fits its values, and descriptions wrap into readable lines.

r0A.why: Descriptions have comfortable space, but several flags break across lines, interrupting comparison of the identifiers.

ref_equal.why: Equal-looking columns waste space on short Type and Default values, leaving descriptions narrow and breaking both prose and flags across many lines.

ref_auto.why: The description column reads comfortably, but several flags split across lines despite the available width.

raw.unsure: C and E appear nearly identical at this resolution; any small width difference does not materially change their visible wrapping.

ref_auto.why: The descriptions have comfortable space, but three flag identifiers wrap across lines, making them harder to scan and copy.

r0B.why: The narrow flag column breaks identifiers into two or three lines, including a separated leading double hyphen; the extra description space does little to offset that.

r0A.why: Descriptions read comfortably, but several flag identifiers wrap, weakening the first column as a scanning anchor.

ref_equal.why: The type and default columns have excessive empty space while the narrow description column forces heavy wrapping; several flags also wrap.

r0C.why: Flags and defaults remain intact, compact type and default columns are easy to compare, and descriptions wrap naturally into two lines.

raw.unsure: A and C appear nearly identical at the displayed scale; any small width difference does not materially affect their ratings.

provenance.note: AI visual design judgement; not a human reading study
